hero_kpi_rationale: The Streaming segment is the primary driver of growth and strategic transformation for WBD, with HBO Max at the core of revitalizing the economic model amid linear decline.

kpis.explanation_en: Number of subscribers to HBO Max and other streaming services of the group.
kpis.description: The streaming subscriber base increased by 13% in 2025, driven by the international expansion of HBO Max, rising from 116.9 million in 2024 to 131.6 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in streaming subscribers driven by global expansion of HBO Max despite challenging sector environment.

kpis.explanation_en: Revenue from fees paid by distributors (cable, satellite, streaming).
kpis.description: Revenue declined by 2% in 2025, impacted by a 9% drop in domestic linear subscribers, partially offset by a 3% increase in domestic affiliate rates and 13% growth in streaming subscribers.
kpis.signal: Partial stabilization despite decline in linear subscribers, offset by increased affiliate rates and streaming growth.

kpis.explanation_en: Revenue from the sale of advertising space on linear and digital platforms.
kpis.description: Declined by 11% in 2025, primarily due to a 25% drop in audience on domestic linear channels, partially offset by an increase in HBO Max ad-lite subscribers.
kpis.signal: Sharp advertising revenue decline driven by 25% collapse in domestic linear network audiences, partially offset by…

kpis.explanation_en: Revenue from the production and licensing of films, series, games, and sports rights.
kpis.description: Declined by 7% in 2025, affected by an unfavorable comparison with the $576 million in sub-licensing revenue from Olympic rights in Europe in 2024, as well as lower game revenues.
kpis.signal: Revenue decline reflects unfavorable comparison with non-recurring Olympic rights sublicensing in 2024 and lower…

kpis.explanation_en: Operating profit after costs, but before interest and taxes.
kpis.description: Shifted from an operating loss of $10.032 billion in 2024 to a profit of $738 million in 2025, driven by reduced depreciation and restructuring charges.
kpis.signal: Return to operating profitability after massive losses driven by reduced depreciation and amortization charges.

kpis.explanation_en: Expense related to the amortization of intangible assets, particularly content rights.
kpis.description: Decreased by 19% in 2025, down from $7.037 billion in 2024, due to lower amortization of content rights following prior asset impairments.
kpis.signal: Marked reduction in depreciation and amortization reflecting lower asset base following prior period impairments.

kpis.description: Declined by 9% in 2025, reflecting the structural shift toward streaming, with domestic linear subscribers falling from 65.2 million in 2024 to 59.2 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Continued cord-cutting trend reflecting structural shift from traditional television to streaming platforms.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.summary: The company is exposed to cybersecurity risks that could impact its operations and reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to cybersecurity risks including attacks on its systems and data. While cybersecurity is important, language in the filing is standard for media companies with digital platforms.

risks.title: Litigation
risks.summary: The company is subject to litigation that could impact its operations and reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The company is involved in legal proceedings, but no specific material litigation mentioned in the filing demonstrates elevated risk beyond typical industry exposure.

risks.title: Regulation
risks.summary: The company is subject to regulations that could impact its operations and reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to standard regulations common to media and entertainment companies operating globally, including data protection and cybersecurity requirements.

risks.title: Competition
risks.summary: The company operates in a highly competitive environment that could impact its market share and revenues.
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in an intensely competitive environment across streaming, linear television, and film production, with significant competitive pressures from major tech and entertainment competitors.

risks.title: Multiemployer Pension Plans
risks.summary: The company's participation in multiemployer pension plans could result in liabilities affecting costs and cash flows.
risks.score_rationale: The company participates in multiemployer defined benefit pension plans, which could subject it to liabilities if plans become underfunded or if the company withdraws participation.

risks.title: Linear Television Decline
risks.summary: Ongoing structural decline in linear television represents a significant challenge to traditional revenue streams and business model.
risks.score_rationale: Structural decline in linear television viewership (25% audience decline in domestic networks in 2025) and subscribers (9% decline) represents a fundamental shift in consumer behavior away from traditional television.

risks.title: Geopolitics
risks.summary: The company operates in a complex geopolitical environment that could impact its operations and reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The company operates globally and is exposed to geopolitical risks, but no specific material geopolitical issues are highlighted in the filing.

risks.title: Technology
risks.summary: The company is exposed to technology risks related to streaming platforms and digital content delivery.
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to technology risks including streaming platform reliability and digital content distribution, but these are managed through standard operational practices.

ai_positioning.summary: WBD does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
